title: Flu Hospitalizations Top 10,000 in a Week for the First Time This Season, CDC Reports
excerpt: Flu hospitalizations in the United States topped 10,000 in a single week for the first time this season, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Preven
content:
Flu hospitalizations in the United States topped 10,000 in a single week for the first time this season, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's latest FluView report.

U.S. hospitals reported 11,734 laboratory-confirmed flu admissions in the week ending Nov. 14 — up 22 percent from 9,584 the week before, the CDC reported in FluView Week 45, published Nov. 20.

The hospitalization rate rose to 3.5 per 100,000 people, up from 2.8. Adults 65 and older had the highest rate, at 10.6 per 100,000, followed by children 4 and younger at 4.0 per 100,000.

The cumulative hospitalization rate reached 12.0 per 100,000 — the highest for Week 45 since the 2010-11 season, according to the CDC.

The CDC estimates at least 3.7 million illnesses, 50,000 hospitalizations and 2,800 deaths from flu so far this season. Those are modeled estimates, not counted cases, and they are up sharply from a week earlier, when the estimates stood at 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations and 2,100 deaths.

Seven children have died from flu this season, including two more reported in the latest week, the CDC said.

Flu accounted for 2.4 percent of emergency department visits, and outpatient visits for flu-like illness reached 3.8 percent — above the 2.9 percent national baseline for a second straight week.

Texas is among the 10 states with high flu activity, along with California, Colorado, Georgia, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee and Washington. The CDC counts 11 jurisdictions at high or very high levels of flu-like illness.

Of influenza A viruses subtyped in Week 45, 96.4 percent were A(H1N1)pdm09. One A(H5) virus was detected — a single laboratory finding, not an outbreak.

Looking ahead, the CDC's FluSight forecast predicts 9,200 to 36,100 new flu admissions in the week ending Dec. 5, Thanksgiving week. The CDC cautions that activity is higher than typically observed at this time of year, but an earlier rise does not necessarily mean a higher peak or a more severe season. Its preliminary severity assessment remains low for all age groups.

The next FluView report, covering Week 46, is delayed until Nov. 30 because of Thanksgiving.

This is an update to Webb Watch 956's Nov. 21 report on the CDC's Week 44 flu data.

Sources: CDC FluView, Week 45, Nov. 20, 2026; Becker's Hospital Review, Nov. 20, 2026; CDC FluSight forecast.
